content_sections.title: Key Findings:
content_text: *Genetic test results are reported based on the recommendations of American College of Medical Genetics # Due to lack of clinical evidence for this variant, it is classified as variant of uncertain significance.
Variant Interpretation & Clinical correlation:

EHMT1 :c.1204G>T; The submitted sample shows Heterozygous variant in Exon 7 of gene  EHMT1  (chr9: g.137752364G>T). A missense variant “G” to “T” detected at nucleotide position 1204 leading to change in amino acid sequences from Valine to Leucine at codon 402. In silico predictions: Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) Score is uncertain. Population frequency and Internal database :  The p.Val402Leu variant is novel (not in any individuals) in gnomAD All. The p.Val402Leu variant is novel (not in any individuals) in 1kG All. This variant is absent in our internal database.
Clinical Indication:

Eshaal Amir presented with meningitis, developmental history was sitting at 6 month, walking at 18 month, speech single word started with meaning, poor eye contact, poor socialization, sleep very disturbed, hyperactive, no seizures. MRI brain - normal.

content_sections.title: General Content / Notes
content_text: Based on above evidence, this variant (EHMT1:c.1204G>T) is classified as  Uncertain significance  variant.

EHMT1 Gene Phenotype Description : Kleefstra syndrome-1 (KLEFS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EHMT1 gene (607001), which is located within the region of the chromosome 9q34.3 deletion syndrome. Submicroscopic subtelomeric deletions of chromosome 9q are associated with a recognizable intellectual developmental syndrome. Common features in patients with 9q subtelomeric deletion syndrome are severely impaired intellectual development, hypotonia, brachy(micro)cephaly, epileptic seizures, flat face with hypertelorism, synophrys, anteverted nares, everted lower lip, carp mouth with macroglossia, and heart defects (Harada et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2004; Stewart et al., 2004; Neas et al., 2005).

KCNC3 :c.1760C>G; The submitted sample shows Heterozygous variant in Exon 2 of gene  KCNC3  (chr19: g.50323193G>C). A missense variant “C” to “G” detected at nucleotide position 1760 leading to change in amino acid sequences from Proline to Arginine at codon 587. In silico predictions: Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) Score is uncertain. Population frequency and Internal database :  The p.Pro587Arg variant is observed in 3/22,638 (0.0133%) alleles from individuals of gnomAD South Asian background in gnomAD All. The p.Pro587Arg variant is novel (not in any individuals) in 1kG All. This variant is absent in our internal database.

KCNC3 Gene Phenotype Description : Spinocerebellar ataxia-13 (SCA13) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KCNC3 gene (176264) on chromosome 19q13. Spinocerebellar ataxia-13 (SCA13) is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by slowly progressive gait and limb ataxia and dysarthria. Age at onset ranges from childhood to adulthood. Other features, including intellectual impairment, oculomotor disturbances, and pyramidal signs, are variable (Herman-Bert et al., 2000; Subramony et al., 2013).
Case Specific Recommendations: 1. Segregation analysis of the variant by Sanger /Exome sequencing is recommended.

Recommendations  Genetic counseling is advised for interpretation on the consequences of the variant(s).  We recommend confirming the presence of these variants by Sanger /Exome Sequencing.  Segregation analysis of the variant by Sanger /Exome sequencing is recommended.  The significance/classification of the variants might change based on parental and family members genetic testing.  For questions about this report, or for assistance in locating nearby genetic counseling services, please contact the Laboratory:  contact@sngenelab.com .  If results obtained do not match the clinical findings, additional testing should be considered as per referring clinician's recommendation.

EHMT1 Gene Phenotype Description : Kleefstra syndrome-1 (KLEFS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EHMT1 gene (607001), which is located within the region of the chromosome 9q34.3 deletion syndrome. Submicroscopic subtelomeric deletions of chromosome 9q are associated with a recognizable intellectual developmental syndrome. Common features in patients with 9q subtelomeric deletion syndrome are severely impaired intellectual development, hypotonia, brachy(micro)cephaly, epileptic seizures, flat face with hypertelorism, synophrys, anteverted nares, everted lower lip, carp mouth with macroglossia, and heart defects (Harada et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2004; Stewart et al., 2004; Neas et al., 2005).
